reviews.review_msg: very knowledgeable, prepare to have your perspective changed. If you are passionate about studying Feminism, Racism, Colonialism ect. this is the class for you. WITH THAT SAID this is by no means an easy course. Attendance is taken, readings are mandatory, & assignments are written in class to avoid AI. Can be a tough grader, but she is wonderful.

The grading criteria for this class was all over the place. She is a very tough grader and will give similar grades to very different levels of work. She does want everyone to understand the material and gives an engaging lecture, but I just was not a fan of this class and the way it was graded.

Mariam is an amazing prof, she cares about her students and their learning. The assignments and in class essays weren't hard but you do need to do the readings or you will fall behind in discussions. Overall great course, and the lectures are very informative and engaging. the only down side is that its a 3 hour lecture so not everyone likes that

Brilliant. You will learn so much, and you don't have to be an expert in the field of study to do well. They care about their students success and are so excited to teach their material. As long as you are invested and complete the work, you're going to do at least okay, but probably well.

She is a fantastic prof who is understanding and approachable. She has more assignments but allows you to have more chances to do better. Quizzes are done in class but the occasional sick is okay. She engages in good discussion. Generally enjoyed it.

Sitara is a VERY intelligent and a passionate instructor, that much was clear. I found I enjoyed listening to her but not learning from her. Both the assigned readings and language that she used were challenging and undigestible. truly, it was frustrating. She had told the class that it was the only way to present the material, but I beg to differ
Thuy is a great prof, lectures were incredibly relevant and interesting. Assignments were fair. Class is easy to do well in if you simply do the work and care about the content.

Thuy is amazing. She cared for my work, especially my writing, and wanted me to succeed as did I. It hurts my heart to see the poor ratings. Students complained about the course being difficult because it is a 200 level course. Readings are long because 1/week course. Expand your knowledge and ways of thinking with this course. Thuy is great.

Fall 2023 3h course: Long weekly/hard to understand readings irrelevant to lecture, no set rubric/grading system, doesn't respond to emails despite encouraging it, instructions inconsistent -- following them is pointless bc she'll dock marks for things she never told you & doesn't give feedback

Oh my goodness I thought that GSWS professors had to go through rigorous training before teaching but it seems like this is not the case for her. She does not know what the lectures are about, the readings are incredibly difficult to digest and have nothing to do with the class material. Never take a class with her.

Everything felt super vague and unclear. The lectures were so long and usually it was completely unnecessary for the class to keep going (nothing important was being said, mostly rambling). The professor is a really sweet human being, but I think even she didn't know what she was talking about most times.

Everything is unclear and vague. English is not her first language I didn't understand a word she said. She's constantly contradicting herself when you ask questions. She doesn't respond to emails. No rubric no instructions. 30-page readings. hard marking because she contradicts herself and if you do what she says then marks you wrong for it.

took this as a 3h course in Fall 2023 | +ve: easy to connect w | -ve: pre-class readings are boring and incomprehensible even after lectures; tends to drone on bc English is not her first language; INCONSISTENT INSTRUCTIONS in class vs Canvas (no rubrics); sometimes does not respond to emails when you ask her a question; painfully vague feedback
